text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: An institutional records office files ordinary paperwork by assigning a matter identifier, indexing the document type, noting the account and date fields present on the intake form, and routing it to the appropriate review queue for standard processing.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a digital ticket document to a resale channel, stating intent to produce multiple copies of that document and sell them. The actor described transmitting copies to a buyer with the purpose of gate entry, and stated intent to prevent refund, chargeback, or identification follow-up on the account.

3) Materials/access observed: One digital ticket document for a sold-out event; a resale channel listing; the ticket's transfer and gate-scan fields; the buyer's account record; the event's refund and chargeback processing records; and the issuer's identity-verification records.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple identical ticket documents issued from a single account within a short window; repeated transfers of the same document identifier to distinct buyer accounts; gate-scan attempts on a document already marked redeemed; refund and chargeback requests tied to duplicate ticket serials; and identity-verification flags raised on the seller account post-transaction.
